key_insight: As synthetic training budgets grow, increasing tool and database diversity improves tool-use agent generalization more effectively than adding more tasks.
engineering_relevance: Agent training pipelines should control environment composition, prioritizing broader tools, databases, and task complexity when scaling synthetic data.
method: Use SynthAPI to independently control tool, task, and database diversity.
Systematically vary synthetic environment composition across model sizes.
Fit a scaling law to predict downstream generalization from environment scale and composition.
evidence_signal: The study covers 458,752 tasks and 849 trained models across four model sizes; agents scaled using its findings outperform models trained on prior-work data across four evaluation benchmarks.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether the scaling law transfers to production tools, unseen domains, or model sizes beyond those studied.
paper_title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
